title: Citigroup CEO Says AI Spending Isn't Slowing Down Despite Higher Interest Rates
key_facts: Jane Fraser, Citigroup chief executive, spoke on the third-quarter earnings call on Tuesday 13 October.
She said Citigroup is not seeing a slowdown in investment in the broader AI ecosystem despite higher rates.
She said 'There's simply not enough compute' and energy shortages remain a bottleneck.
About 14,000 Citi engineers use Devin, its primary agentic coding tool.
New product launches are 30% to 40% faster with AI.
Citigroup reported third-quarter net income of $5.2 billion, up 17%, and revenue of $23.8 billion, up 8%.
quote_evidence: "We're not seeing a slowdown in investment in the broader AI ecosystem," Fraser said during Tuesday's third-quarter earnings call.
"There's simply not enough compute," she added, noting that energy shortages remain a bottleneck requiring further investment.
why_it_matters_hint: A big bank's chief executive reports that AI investment is holding up despite higher rates.
